g1_neg#1.killer: share of attention mass outside the set read at full precision (top 2% of tokens + 4 sinks + 64 recent tokens), at 32k CoT, under the idea's own rule (tail mass × 2-bit value error ≤ 1e-3)
g1_neg#1.why: The coverage it needs from the top 2% is above what published long-CoT sparsity data supports, and even if that held it saves only about 10–20% over NVFP4 because it stores as many bits.

g1_rf2#2.killer: PCIe time per decode step to fetch the top-256 residuals, against the HBM read time saved compared with NVFP4 (archetype B, 8B, batch 10, 32k). Each layer's top-k depends on that layer's query, so the fetch cannot be prefetched
g1_rf2#2.why: The PCIe residual fetch costs more decode time than the 2-bit HBM reads save over NVFP4, and the quality gain comes from only 256 of 131k tokens (0.2%).

g1_ledger#2.killer: attention mass covered by the top 2% of pages on long CoT (the idea's own threshold)
g1_ledger#2.why: Its 99%-coverage-at-2% condition fails by about 6× on published long-CoT budgets, and the best-case gain over NVFP4 is about 11–23%.

g1_mech#3.killer: share of KV heads that can be K4V4 within a 2.1-bit average (group-128 FP16 scale/zero, 0.25 bit/value, a favourable assumption)
g1_mech#3.why: The 2.1-bit budget leaves room for only 14% retrieval-grade heads where GQA models need about 50%, and 1-bit min-max values give 1.31 relative RMS error (measured), worse than zeroing the value.

g1_rf1#3.killer: Decode time per token per head. Keys are stored in the KLT basis and RoPE is applied after dequantization, so the 128×128 basis cannot be folded into the query. Each cached key has to be rebuilt with a 128×128 matmul: 32,768 FLOP for 40 B read, or 819 FLOP/byte. The H100 ridge point is 295 FLOP/byte, so this part is compute-bound
g1_rf1#3.why: The 2.5-bit memory saving is mostly lost to the key-rebuild compute that comes from applying RoPE after dequantization, so at realistic tensor-core use decode attention gets slower than NVFP4 (values are fine, since their basis folds into the output). The AM/GM gain on real pre-RoPE keys is still unmeasured and needs a real-model KV dump.

g1_neg#3.killer: Attention-logit MSE at 2 bits relative to 4-bit scalar codes. Logit error equals
g1_neg#3.why: The idea's own criterion fails by 6× even at the rate-distortion limit, and per-token Viterbi encoding costs more than the bandwidth it saves.

g1_mech#1.killer: Effective number of attended tokens (N_eff) in retrieval heads
g1_mech#1.why: Subtractive dither removes bias (measured mean error −9e-5 vs −9e-4) but leaves MSE the same (0.302 vs 0.304), and retrieval heads do not average enough tokens to hide a 6 dB value SNR.

g1_ledger#1.killer: AIME24 accuracy change at 32k with 2-bit values
g1_ledger#1.why: The bit accounting holds (3.06 b keys + 2.06 b values + FP8 sinks and window ≈ 2.6 b, 6.1×) and the rotation is sound, but the 2-bit values are the very component that published long-CoT results penalize. The proposed 2-GPU-hour AIME test on R1-Distill-Qwen-7B is the right deciding experiment and needs a real model.
